course.title: Operating Machine Learning and Language Model Systems
course.tagline: Run models, assistants and agents in production as versioned releases that are gated, observed and safe to roll back
course.description: Participants run three systems of a fictional electricity distribution company in production: a fault-risk classifier retrained on monthly batches with planted drift, a field-crew assistant with retrieval and two tools, and an outage-ticket agent. They version everything that changes behaviour as one release unit, build pipelines with validation and promotion gates, release through canary stages with automatic rollback, trace requests, monitor drift and online quality, and keep the agent alive through crashes and runaway loops. Evaluators come ready-made from AE-303.
course.audience: Practitioners. Engineers who have completed the level 200 set or can show equivalent work: a deployed model or language model application they built and can explain.
prerequisites: AE-205 Deploying AI Services: Containers, Serving and Monitoring
AE-203 Building Applications on Language Models
Builds a container image and a continuous-integration workflow
Reads an evaluation report with pass rates and intervals
Has built a tool-calling agent, as in AE-302 or equivalent

Setup: a laptop CPU with uv, or Google Colab; a free OpenRouter key is optional, since every lab also runs on a scripted stand-in model. Nothing downloads a model. Run 00_setup_check before Day 1; see labs/README.md.
course.format_note: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task

outcomes.text: Prepare a release manifest that versions data, code, configuration, model, prompt, retrieval index and tool schemas as one unit, given two runs of the three systems that behave differently
outcomes.evidence: a manifest and the unrecorded change found between the runs

outcomes.text: Build a retraining pipeline, started by a drift or schedule trigger, with data validation and a promotion gate that compares challenger and champion overall and by region, given monthly feeder batches, one of them corrupt and one drifted
outcomes.evidence: a triggered run that promotes on the drifted batch and stops on the corrupt one, with registry lineage

outcomes.text: Deliver language model changes through an evaluation gate and a canary stage with an automatic rollback trigger, given a prompt edit, a model swap and an index refresh, one of which regresses
outcomes.evidence: logs showing two releases shipped and one rolled back on a stated metric

outcomes.text: Configure request tracing, drift monitors and online evaluation with a review queue, and tune alert thresholds, given a replayed month of traffic with two planted shifts
outcomes.evidence: a dashboard, alert rules and a note on shifts found and false alarms removed

outcomes.text: Diagnose an agent incident by replaying recorded traces and fix it with idempotent tools, durable state or a budget, given a recorded failure of the ticket agent
outcomes.evidence: the failure reproduced, a fix and a new regression case

outcomes.text: Measure cost per successful outcome and resource use for each system and set budget alerts, given a month of token, compute and outcome logs
outcomes.evidence: a cost table by system and team, with alert rules

case_study.name: Wahaj Electricity Distribution Company
case_study.summary: Wahaj is a fictional electricity distributor with six regions and 4,800 feeders that runs three systems: a feeder fault-risk classifier retrained on monthly batches, Nabd, a field-crew assistant over the maintenance manuals with two tools, and Mubadir, an outage-ticket agent. Participants version, gate, release, observe and repair all three on synthetic data generated with a fixed seed: twelve monthly batches with one corrupt and one drifted, two versions of the manuals, a replayed month of traffic with two planted shifts, recorded agent traces with one incident, and a month of cost logs.

days.label: Capstone
days.title: Capstone: a release week and its defence
days.subtitle: Eight minutes per participant: the release log, the runbook and one injected fault diagnosed live; questions are inside the eight minutes

capstone.summary: A simulated release week in which a corrupt batch, a provider model update and an agent incident arrive; the participant gates, ships or rolls back each and submits a public repository with pipeline logs, a release log and a runbook, then defends it for eight minutes while the assessor injects one further fault
capstone.submission: A public GitHub repository with the pipeline logs, the release log, the runbook and timestamped trace files of the release week, built from the starter in labs/capstone/. Then an eight-minute live defence in which the assessor injects one further fault and the participant diagnoses it from traces and logs.
